suggestions.title: Open at 1–2 reps in reserve, not 0 — a rated 0 is what froze abs

apply.to: Open every lift at 1–2 RIR and log it: abs at 1 RIR next lower day releases its hold, rows 180 at 2 RIR next upper day releases its

rationale.science: Sets stopped 1–3 reps short of failure produce the same hypertrophy as sets to failure at markedly lower fatigue cost, and on a deficit the priority is defending load rather than accumulating failure work (Schoenfeld 2017; Robinson 2024; Grgic 2021).
rationale.data: You rated five of six openers on 8/7 — the first rated session since 8/3 — and abs went in at 0. Its rirHist is now [2,0,0], holdFlag is true, and your feed reads 'ABS — RIR 0 TWICE · load HELD until an honest session lands'. Rows carries the same flag off [0,0]. Same session: hack opened at 2 and went 32 reps to 36, extension opened at 1 and debuted 155 × 8,9, abs opened at 0 and went 41 reps to 40.
rationale.relationship: Your app's governor reads only the opener. Two consecutive 0s freeze the load however good the reps are, and a single opener at 1 or better releases it — the release is written into progressStep, not into a coach's judgement. My 8/7 card asked you to rate set one and never named a target, which is why a correctly-followed card cost you a lift.

suggestions.predict: Abs opens at 1 RIR on your next lower day and abs.holdFlag flips to false with an ABS — HOLD RELEASED feed row, putting 105 back in reach. Rows opens at 2 RIR on your next upper day and does the same, with 185 back off 10,10. Grade both on holdFlag, not on reps. If an opener goes in at 1 or better and either flag stays true, the rule is not what I read in your source and I will say so.

suggestions.title: Stagger the two upper-day set additions — raise it with your coach before you train

rationale.science: Weekly set volume shows diminishing returns — highest per-set payoff at roughly 5–10 sets, less above it (Pelland 2025, 67 studies / 2,058 participants) — and on an energy deficit the marginal set costs recovery that is already scarce, which is the case for living in the high-return tier rather than stacking additions (Schoenfeld 2017).
rationale.data: You approved three owner's calls on 8/7: hams 4→6, chest 6→8, rear delt 6→8 weekly sets. Hams has run once (120 × 11,9,11). Chest and rear delt have not run at all — they both land on your next upper day, which is also press 250's ownership repeat. Your own app flagged the risk on the cards: recovery reads WATCH and three simultaneous experiments raise the odds any single read comes back 'did not convert'.
rationale.relationship: Your app restarts each lift's volume-conversion window at the change and grades each one on its own bar. Two changes on the same upper session, with the press set fractionally billing triceps and front delts as well, means the reads overlap and none of them answers cleanly. Splitting them by a week costs one week and buys three separate verdicts instead of one blurred one.

suggestions.predict: Take one of the two upper-day additions this week and the other next, and each lift's conversion read comes back attributable. Take both at once and expect at least one 'did not convert' you cannot assign a cause to — and a press ownership repeat confounded by a fourth set on the same day.
